Event: `e297d72ad69930a75593835f0fb9f215` · 2026-09-26T07:18:49Z

> P1 continued
> RED-8 memory-layout.md:387-389: the residual is softened. The loader maps the physmap to the end of RAM (loader/src/paging.rs:46, ram.end.div_ceil(LARGEST_LEAF)), but the kernel window stops at PHYSMAP_SIZE (arch/riscv/physmap.rs:17), and frames go lowest first (mem.rs:238). With Sv39 RAM of 128-254 GiB the machine boots, then panics at run time the first time a frame above 128 GiB is used, which a process can cause by allocating. The page says it 'stops at boot'.

### Red team · Answer

Event: `4c5425847cc311371254e27d60898d15` · 2026-09-26T07:45:13Z

> ipc.md:149-154: the decoder's refusal list is incomplete; the handle mask is checked against MAX_MSG_HANDLES, not the handles supplied (libs/sys ret.rs:166); and Request::reply hands the request back on error (rt ipc.rs:335). (All from a sub-reviewer, not re-opened by me.)
> ipc.md:211 (R2 status gap): redoubt-client.rs:148-167 fills WAIT_CAP for one group only (one system budget, account 0). Grouping by label set and by budget is model-only too, but the gap names only 'turns between several groups'.
> budgets.md:279 (R6 status gap): it omits that the saved-context pages (1 on rv32, 2 on rv64) are pinned by no case, which objects.md:155 states.
> memory.md:50: the gap's reason is wrong. dma-reset-reuse does see which frames it gets (reuse by physical address); it never reads them to check they are zero.
> memory.md:69: touch-beyond-ram exhausts RAM (32 MiB guest), not the placement area. Nothing attacks first-fit from the last run, wrap-around, the 4 MiB message area, or an oversize request.
> memory.md:71-75: the search range excludes last_start (mem.rs:363); a run that fits only at the very end, or a request equal to the whole area, is OutOfMemory.
> memory.md:87: return-lent-unmapped runs map_fixed on rv32 too.
> processes.md:135-138: process_start omits TooLarge from table_growth (process.rs:457) and NotPermitted for no budget (:455).
> processes.md:172: the creator's budget stays one page up (the process object) until the notice is taken or dropped (process.rs:277, 620).
> If your fixes cover these, then nothing else was meant.
